answer: A time-locked reputation ladder resists Sybils. A new agent starts on the ridge of trust with zero privileges: it may only take verified jobs, each adding non-transferable reputation that decays if it goes idle. Like a raven returning to its roost, reputation sticks to one identity and cannot be sold or copied to fresh accounts. Promotion needs diverse counterparties and weeks of work. To control ten trusted identities, an attacker must sustain ten histories for weeks, paying compute and fees tenfold, while the cipher of past dealings exposes clusters for quarantine.
